aspect: Everything fails together, which is the point
description: Redundancy assumes independent failures. In war the failures are correlated by design, so every backup plan is disabled by the same event as the plan.
energy_note: No plan B, because B ran on the same grid.

aspect: Schools close and the year is gone
description: In the 2026 war, universities and schools were closed until further notice by directive. A closed school year is not recoverable time for a child; it is a permanent notch in a curve.
time_note: School days lost in one closure.
energy_note: A year removed from a childhood, quietly.
source_name: Supreme National Security Council directive, reported

description: Insulin, antipsychotics, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement. These are the drugs where a two-week gap is a medical event, and pharmacy supply is exactly what a strike or a blockade interrupts first.
money_note: Black-market or substitute pricing during shortage.
energy_note: Rationing your own tablets and doing the arithmetic nightly.

description: The clinic is shut, the pharmacy has queues down the block, and the insulin she has left is enough for nine days if she cuts the evening dose. She cuts the evening dose. Nobody records this anywhere as a war injury.
energy_note: A slow injury that will never be counted as one.

aspect: Income stops but obligations do not
description: Rent, loans and school fees carry on accruing through a period in which no work is possible. The debt created is a war injury that looks, on paper, like personal financial mismanagement.
energy_note: Arriving out of a war already behind.
notes: Cross-reference: assets/text/general excludes ordinary debt as not imposed. This is imposed, and the distinction matters.
